text:
olivia: heads up — west2 cilium 1.25 rollout completed ~09:12 and we've started seeing GPU job queue slowdowns. p95 east-west latency jumped from ~6ms -> 120-300ms and some pods show readiness flapping. logs show retransmits and TCP checksum errors.
kevin: ugh. any obvious MTU changes during the rollout?
olivia: rollout used default tunnel mode (geneve) and we didn't change MTU configs. nodes report `mtu 1450` still.
devops-bot: Deploy cilium/1.25 applied to cluster-west2 at 2024-11-22T09:12:05Z (canary->all).
nina: can you paste `ip -s link` from a guilty node and a healthy node? also check offload flags — I suspect checksum offload interaction with geneve encapsulation.
olivia: grabbing now — output snippet:
```
# from gpu-node-7
3: geneve0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    RX: bytes 18233489 packets 232124 errors 0 dropped 0 overruns 0
    TX: bytes 19123412 packets 239912 errors 12 dropped 0 overruns 0
    features: tx-checksumming rx-checksumming scatter-gather tcp-segmentation-offload
```
```
# from healthy-node-2
3: geneve0: ... errors 0\n    features: tx-checksumming rx-checksumming scatter-gather tcp-segmentation-offload
```
kevin: errors != 0 on tx side is suspicious. can we see `ethtool -k` and `dmesg | tail`?
sam: Also noticed RDMA jobs show handshake retries for large pages — could be fragmentation or offload causing bad checksums on encapsulated packets. RDMA devices are on different VF-sr drivers, so hairpin and encapsulation matters.
luca: re MTU — if geneve adds 50-60 bytes and MTU left unchanged, packets will fragment. fragmentation+offload combos historically cause checksum-zero problems on some NIC firmwares.
kevin: do we have reproducer? maybe run a small iperf UDP stream between two pods with `--mtu 1400` and compare kernel counters pre/post.
olivia: started iperf test between gpu-pod-a and gpu-pod-b, here's top of `/proc/net/dev` after a minute: `tx_errors +15` on geneve0, and kernel logs show: `NETDEV_TX: droq_xmit failed, tx_desc_err` on ixgbevf.
nina: that points at VF driver hitting checksumming/segmentation offload bug. Cilium 1.25 changed how it sets GSO/TSO on geneve iface (we left default). Can you try toggling `ethtool -K geneve0 tx off sg off gso off` on one node as quick mitigation?
olivia: trying on gpu-node-7 now...
(devops-bot): Command executed on gpu-node-7: `ethtool -K geneve0 tx off sg off gso off` — success.
kevin: after toggling, any change to packet errors or p95?
olivia: p95 dropped to ~15-30ms for iperf, tx_errors stopped increasing after ~20s. jobs started to drain and scheduler stopped requeuing.
sam: OK that's a solid mitigation. We should roll a hotfix: either set Cilium tunnel iface offload toggles via DaemonSet post-up hook or pin Cilium to a build that doesn't toggle offloads.
luca: long term we should test driver + offload combos in our CI (ixgbevf, mellanox vf, azure accelerated) with encap modes. This will be a recurring pattern when we bump CNI.
kevin: open an incident ticket and mark P2 (impact on GPU throughput, degraded within 1 region). include repro steps and mitigation commands. assign to eng-infra + eng-runtime to coordinate with Cilium upstream.
olivia: opening ticket now and will attach `dmesg`, `ethtool -k` and `kubectl logs` for the affected pods. also scheduling a short rollback window if 1.25 continues to fail in west2.
nina: FYI, Cilium slack thread mentions similar checksum issue with 1.25 in kernel 5.15 when geneve+VF offloads enabled — linking later. :eyes:
kevin: can we also check autoscaler behavior? we temporarily throttled GPU autoscaler to avoid spin-up storms; if nodes go NotReady we may create excess capacity and cost.
olivia: noted — disabled scale-up for the west2 GPU pool for 30m. will re-enable once stable.
sam: thanks. action items: (1) mitigation DaemonSet to disable offloads (olivia), (2) open ticket + incident doc (kevin), (3) run CI matrix for encap+drivers (luca), (4) upstream Cilium bug report and ask for patch or config option (nina).
kevin: adding: consider forcing `host-device` mode on a small canary to avoid geneve for RDMA-heavy workloads as a short-term routing policy.
olivia: ack. I'll post status updates in this thread as I have them. :thumbsup:
